name: Blog Porter – Blog Migration Importer
author: Azor Studio

sections.description:
Blog Porter moves your existing blog posts into WordPress without manual copy-paste or XML exports, while preserving the available SEO elements. Connect a supported platform, review every post before anything is touched, then import through your own WordPress dashboard.

If you have 150 posts, that review-then-import workflow saves more than a full day of work over doing it by hand.

Key migration features

  • WordPress-native. Once migrated, your posts behave like native WordPress content. Blog Porter creates Gutenberg blocks directly in your site, fully editable and without shortcodes.
  • Images move too. The Blog Porter plugin downloads available inline and featured images into your WordPress Media Library while it imports.
  • SEO-friendly migration. Keep the content signals you need for a careful move: titles, slugs, publish dates, links, and formatting.

Why use Blog Porter?

  • Everything happens in WordPress. Install the free plugin, connect the blog you are moving, review it, complete checkout, and manage the import in one place.
  • Review before you pay. Blog Porter analyses the source and lets you review the detected posts before the one-time migration checkout.
  • No XML file or extra migration tool to manage. Blog Porter prepares your migration and delivers it straight into WordPress-native, SEO-friendly content.
  • Keep going if an import is interrupted. Progress is saved between small batches. You can pause after the current post, resume later, and retry posts or media that need another attempt.
  • $0.20 per post. Pay once per migration. No account is required and there is no subscription.

Supported blog platforms

Blog Porter supports public blogs from Wix, Blogger, Medium, Squarespace, Webflow, and HubSpot when that platform is enabled by the Blog Porter service. For Medium, you can also provide the ZIP archive supplied by Medium.

See the current source-specific coverage before you start:

  • Wix to WordPress migration
  • Blogger to WordPress migration
  • Medium to WordPress migration
  • Squarespace to WordPress migration
  • Webflow to WordPress migration
  • HubSpot to WordPress migration

Content coverage

Coverage depends on what the source platform makes publicly available.

See the full content coverage table on the Blog Porter website.

Your complete WordPress migration, in five steps

  1. Install and activate Blog Porter on the WordPress site that will receive your blog.
  2. Open Blog Porter from the WordPress admin sidebar and choose the platform you are moving from.
  3. Enter the public blog URL, or upload your Medium archive, then confirm that you own the content.
  4. Review the detected posts and complete the one-time checkout when you are happy to proceed.
  5. Start the import. Blog Porter creates the available posts, taxonomy, and media in WordPress, with progress shown as it works.

Blog Porter is SEO-friendly

Blog Porter preserves available post titles, content, publish dates, slugs, and taxonomy where the source platform makes them available.

That said, Blog Porter does not recreate a source platform’s theme, page design, ecommerce data, custom applications, or redirect configuration. A successful blog migration with Blog Porter alone cannot guarantee rankings: your theme, metadata, internal links, redirects, and indexing settings still need to be reviewed before you switch traffic. If an old URL changes, configure and test a 301 redirect to its new WordPress URL.

Who Blog Porter is for

  • Bloggers and businesses leaving Wix, Blogger, Medium, Squarespace, Webflow, or HubSpot CMS who want full ownership of their content on WordPress.
  • Agencies and freelancers migrating client blogs without hand-copying every post.
  • Writers who want their archive to keep its original dates, slugs, and images.

External service and privacy

Blog Porter handles the source-platform analysis and content preparation behind the scenes, while every migration step is completed from your WordPress dashboard. You do not need to export, upload, or manage a migration file yourself.

When you start a migration, the plugin securely connects to Blog Porter to analyse your blog, prepare the content, and import it into WordPress. You stay in control: review what was found before checkout, then follow the migration progress from your WordPress dashboard.

Blog Porter is a paid, pay-as-you-go service and does not require an account. Migration is $0.20 per post, charged once, with no subscription or recurring fee. Payment is processed by Polar. Service terms and data handling details are available here:

  • Privacy Policy: https://blogporter.com/privacy
  • Terms and Conditions: https://blogporter.com/terms

Trademarks

WordPress is a trademark of the WordPress Foundation. Wix, Blogger, Medium, Squarespace, Webflow, HubSpot, and Polar are trademarks or registered trademarks of their respective owners. Their names are used solely to identify supported services and do not imply endorsement or affiliation.
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate the plugin.
  2. Open Blog Porter from the WordPress admin sidebar.
  3. Review the external-service and privacy information shown in the plugin.
  4. Analyse a supported public blog and complete checkout, or enter an existing Blog Porter export ID.
  5. Let Blog Porter check for existing posts, then start the import or choose whether existing posts should be updated.
sections.faq:
Do I need to upload an XML file?

No. The recommended workflow prepares the migration on Blog Porter and downloads small import batches directly into WordPress. A manual XML export is available only as a fallback when you cannot install plugins on the destination site.

Is Blog Porter free?

The plugin is free to install. Migration is $0.20 per post, charged once, with no subscription or recurring fee. You review the detected content first, then pay the one-time migration fee. No account is required.

Can I see what Blog Porter finds before paying?

Yes. Analyse the supported public blog from the plugin, review the detected posts, and choose which content to migrate before completing checkout.

Can I migrate only selected posts?

Yes. Review the detected posts before checkout and choose which content you want to migrate.

Does it copy images?

Blog Porter copies available inline and featured images into the WordPress Media Library when the source server allows them to be downloaded. The import summary identifies media that needs another attempt.

Can I pause or retry an import?

Yes. Imports can be paused after the current post and resumed later. Posts or media with errors can be retried without duplicating successfully imported posts or attachments.

Can I migrate a large blog?

Yes. Blog Porter imports content in resumable batches, so you can pause, resume, and retry without starting the migration from scratch.

Do I need coding skills or hosting access?

No. Install the plugin, enter your blog URL, review the migration, and import from your WordPress dashboard.

Will Blog Porter preserve my SEO?

Blog Porter preserves available content details such as slugs, publish dates, and taxonomy, but SEO depends on more than the import. Before publishing the new site, review metadata and internal links, then add and test 301 redirects for URLs that change. Blog Porter does not configure redirects automatically.

Does Blog Porter migrate my whole website?

No. Blog Porter is for blog content migrations. It does not recreate your source theme, page layouts, ecommerce data, custom apps, or domain and redirect settings.

What if Blog Porter cannot import something?

The migration summary shows what was imported and highlights posts or media that need another attempt.
sections.changelog:
0.3.67

  • Detects posts already imported by Blog Porter before checkout, so they are excluded by default and are not charged twice.
  • Fixed an issue that could prevent some categories from being imported.

0.3.66

  • WordPress 7.1 compatibility

0.3.65

  • Fixed author detection in WordPress
  • Fixed multi-image galleries from Wix in WordPress

0.3.64

  • Correct the WordPress.org contributor metadata.
